targets.label: Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence)
targets.statement:
Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), paper page 2, with the standing definitions in Section 2.

Let Torus = R/(2 pi Z), with normalized measure dx/(2 pi). Write fhat(k) = (2 pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2 pi) f(x) exp(-ikx) dx, <k> = (1+k^2)^(1/2), and ||f||_(H^s)^2 = sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2s) |fhat(k)|^2. The spaces are completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms; negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. The L2 norm uses the normalized measure. For mean-zero functions, the homogeneous and inhomogeneous norms obey ||f||_(dot H^s) <= ||f||_(H^s) <= 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s) for s >= 0, and 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s) <= ||f||_(H^s) <= ||f||_(dot H^s) for s < 0. Reality means fhat(-k) = conjugate(fhat(k)). Mean zero means fhat(0) = 0. All time suprema concern continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

Let S_t = exp(-t partial_x^3), so (S_t f)hat(k) = exp(i t k^3) fhat(k). Let P_0 be the mean, P = I-P_0. Let D^(-1) = partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (ik)^(-1) at k != 0 and zero at k=0, and D^(-2) = (D^(-1))^2.

The equation (1) is partial_t u + partial_x^3 u = (1/2) partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u_0. The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T]; H^gamma(Torus)) solution obtained by smooth approximation, satisfying the equation distributionally.

The fixed unfiltered time-semidiscrete scheme (2), with no spatial Fourier cutoff, is u^0=u_0 and u^(n+1) = S_tau u^n + F_tau(u^n) + H_tau(u^n), where tau=T/L and
F_tau(f) = (1/6) P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)^2] - (1/6) S_tau P[(D^(-1)f)^2],
H_tau(f) = (1/3) P[(S_tau D^(-1)f) D^(-1)F_tau(f)] + (tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 - (1/54) [S_(tau-s) D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 - (1/(27 tau)) [S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0). This is the full displayed update of the paper, identified there with Li-Wu [1, Eq. (1.4)].

For every T>0, every gamma with 0<gamma<=1, and every R>0, there exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real, mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau_0, the specified scheme satisfies max_(integers 0<=n<=L) ||u(n tau)-u^n||_(L2) <= C tau^gamma. In particular, C and tau_0 are uniform over the entire indicated initial-data ball and independent of L, n and Fourier support. Preserve the exact solution concept and the entire update above; temporary smoothness and proof-only frequency thresholds do not restrict the target or modify the algorithm.

The supplied complete paper is the proof source. Its Section 2.1 identifies the external exact-flow results and sign change; Sections 3 and 4 give its proof of this target. No numerical convergence theorem is assumed as an input. This selection is a source transcription and target freeze, not a proof or an acceptance judgment.
